# `silk/text/regex_shape`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The structure of an ECMAScript Unicode regular expression, read during compilation.

## When to use
Use `RegexShape.of` in static code that needs to know whether a pattern is valid and which
capture groups it has before the program runs, such as a library that types a pattern's
captures. Use `silk.text.regex` to compile and search at run time.

## Details
`RegexShape.of` reads a pattern the way `Regex.compile` does: the same ECMAScript Unicode (`u`)
grammar, the same error messages and offsets, and the same Unicode property names. It builds no
program. Two resource limits are checked only by `Regex.compile`, because only the program
reveals them: too many class ranges and too many nested quantifiers.

A typed pattern names its groups after fields, so a group name here must be an ASCII
identifier written out; a name with a `\u` escape or a non-ASCII character is reported as an
error even though `Regex.compile` accepts it.

Reading a pattern is static work and counts against the static evaluation budget: a run of
plain characters costs a few dozen steps a byte, and a group or quantified term a few hundred,
so patterns of several hundred bytes fit comfortably while one with hundreds of groups does
not.

## Examples
### Read a pattern's groups at compile time
```silk
import silk.core.static_sequence { StaticSequence }
import silk.text.regex_shape { RegexGroup, RegexShape }

static fn secondName() -> string<'static> {
  let shape = RegexShape.of("(?<year>\\d{4})-(?<month>\\d{2})?")
  if !shape.valid {
    compileError(shape.message)
  }
  let month = StaticSequence.at<RegexGroup>(shape.groups, 1)
  if !month.optional {
    compileError("month sits under ?")
  }
  return month.name
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  if secondName() != "month" {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="RegexShape.impl.of"></a>

### Associated function `of`

```silk
pub static fn of(pattern: string) -> RegexShape
```

Reads an ECMAScript Unicode (`u`) pattern as `Regex.compile` would, without compiling it.

#### Details
A valid pattern lists every capture group, named or not, in number order. An invalid one
carries the message and offset `Regex.compile` would report, and `limit` for a pattern
longer than 65,536 bytes, groups nested deeper than 255 levels, or 255 or more captures.
Group names must be ASCII identifiers written out, as the module documentation explains.
